subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake behavior, channel notification behavior, and config/per-spawn API should it own?
rationale: The remaining work adds recovery policy, default/config behavior, mutating child-run control, and user-visible failure handling for existing deployments, so it is not a narrow source repair automation can safely choose alone.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify default versus opt-in behavior, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to sessions.activity and manual kill/reap work.

options.title: Prototype default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused live chat-channel proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer to existing controls
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill yet; rely on runTimeoutSeconds, generic stuck-session recovery, and future manual kill/reap controls until stronger product direction exists.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify default versus opt-in behavior, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to sessions.activity and manual kill/reap work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across diagnostics, subagent control, and config/default surfaces touched by this decision.
